During the day, things will pop into my head out of nowhere. I’ll be at my desk talking to a client about their policy or answering emails, and I suddenly get these images or thoughts that just slam into me. Sometimes it’s related to the accident, sometimes it’s just… disturbing stuff that doesn’t even make sense to me. I don’t want to think about it, but it keeps looping.

I catch myself going back over things in my mind—conversations, details, whether I missed something important—over and over, like I’m trying to undo something or prevent something bad. It doesn’t really help; it just makes me more exhausted and on edge. I’ve been more irritable with my kids on the phone and I avoid driving when I can, but I’m not sure if I’m overreacting or if something’s really wrong.

During the day, I’ll be in the middle of quoting a policy or talking to a customer and suddenly I’m back on that highway—hearing the metal crunch, smelling the smoke, seeing the other driver’s face. It just pops in, and I can’t stop it. These thoughts and images are always about the crash; they’re not random worries about germs or numbers or anything like that. I don’t do any rituals or checking to make them go away—I just kind of freeze or start crying.

At night it’s worse. I keep having these awful dreams where I’m in a pileup or I can’t get out of the car. I wake up sweating, heart racing, sometimes screaming. I dread going to sleep because I know I’ll end up back in that moment again.
